details:
SPACE LEGACY – Project Description

SPACE LEGACY is an interactive educational platform that shares the stories of NASA's abandoned and retired equipment on the Moon and Mars, including rovers, landers, and scientific instruments. Through images, interactive maps, mission timelines, and storytelling, users can explore the equipment's locations, purposes, discoveries, and mission histories.

The project aims to make space exploration history more interesting and accessible while encouraging students to develop an interest in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM). It also preserves the historical and scientific value of space equipment by highlighting how these machines contributed to important discoveries and future space missions.

The platform uses technologies such as HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, and Three.js to create an interactive and engaging experience. NASA Open Data and the NASA Image and Video Library provide reliable information, images, and scientific resources.

SPACE LEGACY is creative because it transforms historical information into an interactive virtual space museum. Instead of simply presenting facts, it tells the journey, achievements, and legacy of each piece of equipment through visual storytelling, interactive maps, timelines, and 3D visualisations.

During development, our team considered several important factors, including information accuracy, user experience, accessibility, educational value, creativity, and scientific relevance. These factors ensure that the platform is informative, engaging, and easy to use.

Ultimately, SPACE LEGACY aims to increase public awareness of space exploration, inspire future generations, and demonstrate that even abandoned space equipment can leave behind a valuable scientific legacy.
